summary_paragraph: A 70-year-old woman with a history of coronary artery disease, prior CABG, and hypothyroidism was admitted for epigastric pain that she recognized as a prior anginal equivalent. The pain began after a mild URI and was associated with bloating and burping, worsening slightly after meals but resolving with sleep. She denied chest pain, shortness of breath, nausea, or vomiting. Initial EKG showed minor changes including T-wave inversion in V1 and ST depression in V2, but cardiac enzymes were negative across three tests. She remained asymptomatic during telemetry monitoring. A chest X-ray showed no acute cardiopulmonary findings. The pain was attributed to gastroesophageal reflux, and she was managed with continued cardiac medications and addition of ranitidine during admission. At discharge, she was advised to start OTC Prilosec, continue her home regimen with adjustments including a switch to metoprolol succinate and reduced atorvastatin dose, and follow up with her primary care provider. Anxiety was noted during admission, and she received supportive care.
problems: Coronary atherosclerosis of unspecified type of vessel, native or graft
